title: What is JVM?
problemStatement: Explain what the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) is and why it is important.

title: JDK vs JRE
problemStatement: Explain the difference between JDK and JRE.

title: What is Inheritance?
problemStatement: Explain inheritance in Java with an example.

title: Method Overloading
problemStatement: What is method overloading? Explain with an example.

title: ArrayList vs LinkedList
problemStatement: Explain the differences between ArrayList and LinkedList.

title: Primitive types and reference types
problemStatement: Explain the difference between primitive values and object references in Java. Give examples and describe what a variable stores in each case.

title: The difference between == and equals
problemStatement: Explain what == compares for primitives and objects, how equals is intended to work, and why String comparisons should usually use equals.

title: static, final, and finally
problemStatement: Explain the different purposes of the static keyword, the final keyword, and a finally block. Include one example of each.

title: Is Java pass-by-value or pass-by-reference?
problemStatement: Explain how Java passes primitive values and object references to methods. Use a short example to show what happens when a method reassigns a parameter versus mutating the referenced object.

title: Java access modifiers
problemStatement: Compare public, protected, package-private, and private access. Explain how package boundaries affect what code can access a member.

title: Abstract class versus interface
problemStatement: Compare abstract classes and interfaces in modern Java. Describe when you would choose each and how a class can use both.

title: Encapsulation and its benefits
problemStatement: Explain encapsulation and show how a Java class can protect its state while exposing a clear public API.

title: Polymorphism and dynamic dispatch
problemStatement: Explain runtime polymorphism in Java. Describe how an overridden method is selected when a superclass reference points to a subclass object.

title: Composition versus inheritance
problemStatement: Compare composition and inheritance. Give an example where composition makes a design easier to change than a deep inheritance hierarchy.

title: The contract between equals and hashCode
problemStatement: State the equals and hashCode contract. Explain what can go wrong when equal objects return different hash codes in a HashMap or HashSet.

title: Why String objects are immutable
problemStatement: Explain String immutability and its benefits for security, sharing, and hash-based collections. Describe how to build a string efficiently in a loop.

title: StringBuilder versus StringBuffer
problemStatement: Compare StringBuilder and StringBuffer, including their thread-safety behavior and when each is appropriate.

title: How HashMap works internally
problemStatement: Describe how HashMap uses hashCode and equals to store and retrieve a value. Explain collisions and what makes a good map key.

title: HashSet and duplicate detection
problemStatement: Explain how HashSet determines whether an element is already present. Describe what an application must implement for custom objects to behave correctly in a set.

title: Fail-fast iterators
problemStatement: What does fail-fast mean for Java collection iterators? Explain why modifying a collection during iteration can cause ConcurrentModificationException and give a safe alternative.

title: Comparable versus Comparator
problemStatement: Compare Comparable and Comparator. Show how to sort the same type by two different fields without changing its natural ordering.

title: When to use List, Set, and Map
problemStatement: Compare the purposes of List, Set, and Map. For each, give a practical use case and explain the key behavior it provides.

title: HashMap versus ConcurrentHashMap
problemStatement: Compare HashMap and ConcurrentHashMap for concurrent access. Explain atomic operations such as computeIfAbsent and when a concurrent map is useful.
keyConcepts: Thread safety, Concurrent collections, Atomic operations

title: Checked and unchecked exceptions
problemStatement: Explain checked versus unchecked exceptions, how the compiler treats them, and how you decide whether an error should be represented by each kind.

title: try-with-resources
problemStatement: Explain how try-with-resources closes resources. Describe the AutoCloseable contract and why this construct is safer than manually closing resources in finally.

title: Can a finally block fail to run?
problemStatement: Explain the normal guarantees and important exceptions for a finally block. Discuss why returning from finally is discouraged.

title: What is type erasure?
problemStatement: Explain type erasure in Java generics and describe one consequence it has for runtime type checks or overloaded methods.

title: Upper-bounded and lower-bounded wildcards
problemStatement: Explain the meanings of ? extends T and ? super T. Use a collection example to show when each bound is useful.

title: Functional interfaces and lambdas
problemStatement: Explain what makes an interface functional and how a lambda expression can implement it. Give an example using a standard Java functional interface.

title: Stream map versus flatMap
problemStatement: Compare map and flatMap in the Stream API. Describe a case where each is appropriate and explain whether stream operations modify the source collection.

title: Intermediate and terminal stream operations
problemStatement: Distinguish intermediate and terminal stream operations. Explain laziness and why a stream cannot normally be reused after a terminal operation.

title: When to use Optional
problemStatement: Explain what Optional represents, show how it can make a return value clearer, and describe why it is usually not a replacement for every nullable field or method parameter.

title: Default methods in interfaces
problemStatement: Why were default methods added to interfaces? Explain how a class handles a conflict when two implemented interfaces provide the same default method.

title: Thread versus Runnable
problemStatement: Compare extending Thread with implementing Runnable or Callable. Explain how a task can be submitted to an executor and how Callable returns a result.

title: synchronized and mutual exclusion
problemStatement: Explain what synchronized protects, what monitor lock is used, and why synchronizing the smallest correct critical section is often preferable.

title: What does volatile guarantee?
problemStatement: Explain visibility and ordering guarantees provided by volatile. Explain why volatile alone does not make a compound operation such as count++ atomic.
keyConcepts: Memory visibility, Atomicity, Java Memory Model

title: Why use an ExecutorService?
problemStatement: Explain how ExecutorService manages submitted tasks compared with creating threads manually. Describe how to shut it down and handle task results.

title: Deadlock and prevention
problemStatement: Define deadlock, describe the conditions that can create one, and give practical techniques to prevent or diagnose deadlocks in Java code.

title: CompletableFuture basics
problemStatement: Explain how CompletableFuture can compose asynchronous tasks. Compare thenApply with thenCompose and describe where exceptions are handled.

title: Stack and heap memory
problemStatement: Describe the typical roles of stack frames and the heap in a Java application. Explain what happens when a method calls another method and creates an object.

title: Garbage collection in Java
problemStatement: Explain how the garbage collector identifies objects that can be reclaimed and why calling System.gc does not guarantee immediate collection.

title: OutOfMemoryError versus StackOverflowError
problemStatement: Compare OutOfMemoryError and StackOverflowError. Give a likely cause for each and describe the first evidence you would inspect when diagnosing them.

title: What does a class loader do?
problemStatement: Explain how a class loader loads classes and describe the parent-delegation model at a high level. Give an example of why class loading matters in an application.

title: PreparedStatement and SQL injection
problemStatement: Explain how PreparedStatement binds values and why it is safer than building SQL with string concatenation. Include a simple database-query example in words.

title: JDBC connection and resource lifecycle
problemStatement: Outline the steps for executing a parameterized JDBC query and explain how connections, statements, and result sets should be closed.

title: Count character frequencies in a string
problemStatement: Write or explain a Java method that counts each character in a string. State how you handle spaces and case, and give the time and space complexity.

title: Remove duplicates while preserving order
problemStatement: Given a list of values, describe a Java solution that removes duplicates while preserving the first-seen order. Explain the collection choice and complexity.

title: Find the first non-repeating character
problemStatement: Design a Java method that returns the first character that appears exactly once in a string. Explain how you preserve the original order and analyze complexity.
